description.summary: Marathon shell integration for toplevel windows

protocol.description:
Lets a client whose windows are Marathon apps (Waydroid's hwcomposer, native apps) take part in the shell's window model: learn which part of its window the shell covers, receive the system back gesture as it happens, and mark windows secure, not focusable or not touchable.
The shell may hide the global from clients it does not trust, such as sandboxed clients from engines other than Marathon's app runner.
Warning! This protocol is Marathon's own and still unstable. Backwards incompatible changes are made by renaming the interfaces with a new version suffix, compatible ones by bumping the interface versions.

interface.name: marathon_surface_manager_v1

description.summary: creates Marathon window state for toplevels

interface.description: A global that adds Marathon window state to xdg_toplevel objects.

entry.name: already_exists
entry.summary: the xdg_toplevel already has a marathon_surface_v1

request.name: destroy
request.description: Objects created through the manager are not affected.

request.name: get_surface

description.summary: create Marathon window state for a toplevel

request.description:
Creates a marathon_surface_v1 for the toplevel. Create it before the toplevel's initial commit: the shell decides how to map the window (activated or not) on that commit, and sends the initial insets with the first configure sequence. Created later, the flags still apply from then on, and the current insets are sent in a new configure sequence.
task_id is the Android task the window belongs to, 0 for a native window. Marathon v1 records it for the shell's task code; it does not yet group windows by it.

arg.name: task_id
arg.summary: task the window belongs to, or 0

interface.name: marathon_surface_v1

description.summary: Marathon window state of one toplevel

interface.description:
Marathon window state of one xdg_toplevel.
The insets and ime_inset events are part of the xdg_surface configure sequence, as xdg_toplevel.configure is: they are sent before the xdg_surface.configure event that completes the sequence, and the client applies them together with the size when it acks that configure. They are sent when their value changes, and once when the object is created; an unchanged value is not sent again.
If the xdg_toplevel is destroyed first, this object becomes inert: its requests are ignored and no events are sent. Destroy it then.

entry.name: invalid_rects
entry.summary: rects is not whole rectangles, or one has a negative size

enum.name: window_flags
enum.description: The default, 0, is an ordinary window.

entry.name: not_focusable
entry.summary: the window never takes keyboard focus nor is activated

entry.name: not_touchable
entry.summary: touch and pointer input pass through the window

entry.name: secure
entry.summary: the window's content is kept out of thumbnails and screenshots

entry.name: hidden
entry.summary: the status area is hidden while the window is in front

enum.name: back_edge
enum.description: The edge the gesture moves away from: left moves rightwards, as a swipe in from the left edge does, right moves leftwards.

request.name: destroy
request.description: The window reverts to the defaults: flags 0, no gesture exclusion, system bars shown. Back reaches it the shell's other way again (a key or the toolkit's own handling).

request.name: set_window_flags
request.description: Replaces the window's flags. Takes effect immediately; it is window management state, not content, so it is not double-buffered.

request.name: set_gesture_exclusion

description.summary: regions where the shell leaves gestures to the window

request.description:
Rectangles, in surface-local coordinates, in which the shell does not start its own edge gestures. rects is an array of int32 quadruples (x, y, width, height); an empty array clears the exclusion. Rectangles rather than a wl_region, because a server cannot read a client's wl_region through the toolkit it is built on, and Android hands the hwcomposer rectangles.
Double-buffered: applied on the next wl_surface.commit.
Marathon v1 stores the exclusion and shows it to the shell's gesture code; no shell gesture consults it yet.

request.name: set_system_bars

description.summary: ask for the status area shown or hidden

request.description: Marathon v1 records the mode but does not act on it: the status area stays shown and the insets stay what they are. A client must lay out from the insets event, never from the mode it asked for.

event.name: insets

description.summary: parts of the window the shell covers

event.description: Distances, in surface-local coordinates, from each edge of the window inwards that shell chrome (the status area, the gesture pill) covers. Marathon lays windows out between its status area and pill, so these are 0 unless a window extends under them.

event.name: ime_inset

description.summary: part of the window the on-screen keyboard covers

event.description: Distance, in surface-local coordinates, from the bottom edge of the window inwards that the on-screen keyboard covers; 0 while it is hidden.

event.name: back_started
event.description: The user started a back gesture over this window. x and y are the touch point in surface-local coordinates and may lie outside the surface: the gesture pill is below the window. Followed by any number of back_progress events, then back_committed or back_cancelled.

event.name: back_progress
event.description: progress runs from 0 (where the gesture began) to 1 (as far as it goes); x and y as in back_started.

event.name: back_committed
event.description: The user went back. Ends a gesture that back_started began, or arrives alone for a back with no gesture (a key). The window does not receive a back key for it.

event.name: back_cancelled
event.description: The gesture that back_started began ended without going back.
